name: Notion
revoke_manual_path: Settings → Notion MCP → All MCP clients
gotcha_copy: Notion has one combined grant with no read/write split. Reauthorization is required after 180 days or 30 days of inactivity. The grant is listed under Settings then Notion MCP, as an MCP client named "kiro" or after the loopback redirect URL the runtime registered (for example 127.0.0.1:5xxxx) rather than Kiro Crew; the Connections page lists workspace apps such as Zapier and never shows it.
revoke_verified_note: user click-verified: grants appear ONLY on Settings → Notion MCP → All MCP clients, a settings-modal page with no dedicated URL, so the link points at the workspace home instead of a deep link that cannot be addressed. www.notion.so is NOT that home -- it redirects a logged-in user to the notion.com marketing site; app.notion.com lands on the workspace, where the manual path applies

name: GitHub
gotcha_copy: GitHub needs a one-time Kiro app registration, and the loopback callback must exactly match the registered URI. Scopes are coarse; prefer the read-only server variant.

name: Linear
gotcha_copy: Linear separates read and write access; Kiro Crew installs the dedicated read-only /mcp/readonly endpoint. Use the MCP Servers tab for write access.

name: Atlassian
gotcha_copy: Covers Jira and Confluence, not Trello. Requires an Atlassian account associated with a Jira or Confluence site (Rovo MCP): without a supported site the consent page reports "Supported sites required" and its Accept button stays disabled. The default grant includes write access; use Edit permissions on Atlassian's consent page to trim it.

name: Stripe
gotcha_copy: Read and write access is controlled at the tool level, not by OAuth scopes. The server is in public preview; use test mode first.

name: Vercel
gotcha_copy: Vercel uses PKCE, refresh, and provider-side revocation. Review the selected team before approving access.

name: GitLab
gotcha_copy: GitLab offers a single mcp scope with no read-only variant, so this grant can write: the same token that reads issues can open issues and merge requests, comment, and run or delete pipelines. Requires GitLab Duo availability set to always on or on by default, beta and experimental features turned on, and MCP server access allowed for the top-level group.
